title: ARIA meters need an accessible name
summary: An element with role meter has no accessible name, so its value has no context. Add aria-label or aria-labeledby saying what it measures.
problem: An element with role="meter" has no accessible name. A meter shows a value within a known range, such as storage used. Without a name, assistive technology announces a number with no hint about what it measures.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear a bare value and cannot tell whether it is disk space, battery or a password score. Sighted users see the nearby label, so the gap affects only people who cannot see it.
steps: Find the element in the scan result.
Add aria-label with what the meter measures, or point aria-labeledby at a visible label that is already on the page.
Make sure aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax are set and match the visual.
Consider the native <meter> element, which provides this semantics without ARIA.
whyItMatters: A value without a label is not information. This rule maps to the WCAG requirement that non-text content has a text alternative, which is a Level A requirement.
howToCheck: Select the element in your browser's accessibility inspector and check that its Name is set. A screen reader should read the name together with the value.
